decisions.choice: Use attribution states unknown, unverified and assigned_by_user. unknown has no usable cluster label. Model clusters produce unverified assignments. Proposals do not change assignment state. A direct user action assigning, merging or confirming a segment creates assigned_by_user in a new revision under I6; clearing an assignment returns it to unknown. Boundary-changing re-diarization carries prior assignments only as unverified proposals. Names and splits are versioned. Notes pin transcript, diarization and speaker revision inputs.
decisions.rationale: Editable identity and names must not change the meaning of saved notes. Every state consumed by notes needs an evidentiary source.

alternatives.tradeoff: Uses fewer records but invalidates old citations and conceals what the model produced.

decisions.consequences: Notes may use confirmed names only for assigned_by_user. Other attribution uses explicitly unverified local labels or remains unattributed. Each note item cites valid segment ranges and timestamps. Renaming or splitting reports drift and offers regeneration. Long notes use the bounded processing contract in D-042.
decisions.reconsider_when: Evaluation supports another clearly defined attribution state without weakening user-confirmation provenance.

decisions.title: Runtime replacement and model retention
decisions.choice: Installations use installed, archived, orphaned_runtime and missing states. Archiving removes execution references while retaining identity, notices and parameter descriptions. Removing an adapter changes affected installations to orphaned_runtime and deletes no assets automatically. Users can archive them or clear their caches. Restoring execution requires matching assets and an available compatible adapter.
decisions.rationale: Historical attribution should not require retaining every executable model forever. Runtime replacement otherwise produces uncontrolled disk growth or unreadable History.

alternatives.option: Retain weights whenever any result references them
alternatives.tradeoff: Keeps reprocessing convenient but lets storage grow with every model tried.

alternatives.option: Delete models when their adapter disappears
alternatives.tradeoff: Reclaims space automatically but removes user assets during an application update.

decisions.consequences: Generic parameter_schema and parameter_display keep old settings readable. The manager reports unique physical bytes, shared bytes, staging and caches, and estimates the effect of archival. Execution leases delay physical cleanup under I3.
decisions.reconsider_when: Users need an explicit automatic archival policy or parameter presentation exceeds the generic descriptor.

decisions.title: Retained context and replay
decisions.choice: Default context persistence records source status, timestamp and digest. An opt-in mode setting retains the exact bounded representation supplied to processing as an owned artifact. Commit its durable file before the context_samples reference. Exclude context from full-text search. Delete it with its session or recording, or through an explicit context-retention operation.
decisions.rationale: Replay needs the actual supplied bytes; a digest can identify a sample but cannot reconstruct it. Retention must have an owner and deletion path.

alternatives.option: Retain every screen and clipboard sample
alternatives.tradeoff: Improves replay availability while accumulating unrelated application content.

alternatives.option: Retain no context under any setting
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplifies storage but prevents deliberate replay with the original context.

decisions.consequences: Reprocessing with absent context requires a visible choice to omit or resample it and creates a new manifest. Resampling never silently claims to reproduce the old result. Logs contain source status and hashes, not context payloads.
decisions.reconsider_when: A broader at-rest protection requirement applies to the recording library.

decisions.title: Service materialization ownership
decisions.choice: Key a materialization by setHash, service kind, runtime revision and cache-format revision. Under a creator lease, register its path before copying into a unique temporary directory inside the service container. Copy assets from passed handles, verify hashes, synchronize files and a completion manifest, then publish without replacement under a per-key broker claim. An existing destination is verified and referenced. Register the completed asset transactionally before releasing the creator lease.
decisions.rationale: Shared content needs shared ownership, while compiled runtime caches may be incompatible across revisions. A completion marker alone cannot protect an active copy from sweeping.

alternatives.tradeoff: Simplifies retention but repeatedly copies large model sets.
Reduces Store work while losing deletion coordination and complete disk accounting.

decisions.consequences: Qualifying installation references and active users retain physical assets under I3. One installation's archival cannot remove another's shared cache. Launch reconciliation cleans dead creators, incomplete copies and unreferenced notices. Size estimates count every runtime-specific copy without assuming compression or cloning.
decisions.reconsider_when: A verified descriptor-loading path or filesystem clone optimization removes copies without changing ownership.

decisions.title: Compatible local models without quality gates
decisions.choice: Compute model identity from a canonical manifest of weights, tokenizer, templates, feature configuration and required companions. Publisher, revision labels, notices and benchmarks may be unknown. Compatibility checks validate asset structure, runtime loading and the result contract. Empty recognition, empty diarization and immediate generation end-of-sequence are valid when contract-shaped. Quality limitations are reported separately.
decisions.rationale: A user-built compatible model should not need invented provenance or a benchmark pack to work.

alternatives.option: Require a known model catalog entry
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplifies setup claims but excludes compatible local models.
Catches some poor models while incorrectly treating legitimate output as runtime incompatibility.

decisions.consequences: Users can browse installations, inspect capabilities, import local model sets and select them in modes. Resource admission still reflects actual hardware. Download offerings require an exact asset and notice inventory. Supplied SpeakerKit component notices do not establish permission to redistribute every weight.
decisions.reconsider_when: A new model family needs additional structural compatibility checks.

decisions.title: Duration-independent working memory
decisions.choice: Every adapter declares finite buffers and a working ceiling expressed through controlled window size, context length and concurrency. Speech uses bounded overlapping windows. Decode reads incrementally under byte credit. Generation uses bounded context and output batches. Long faithful rewrites process transcript spans with overlap used only as context, emitting each source span once. Notes write cited per-window items to disk, then perform bounded fan-in reduction over those items. UI and Store page text and segments. D-043 bounds speaker working state.
decisions.rationale: Queue credit cannot prevent an upstream runtime from retaining the entire input. Each participating process needs an internal bound and resource evidence.

alternatives.tradeoff: Bounds allocation by refusing long work but conflicts with the specification.
Reduces investigation while leaving hidden accumulation unexamined.

decisions.consequences: Output storage and processing time may grow with duration. Window boundaries can affect fidelity and are evaluated. Resource tests use equivalence bounds plus fixed absolute ceilings as defined in verification. A limit breach preserves committed inputs and reports the failed adapter.
decisions.reconsider_when: A runtime exposes a stronger bounded incremental contract or evaluation identifies boundary-related errors.

decisions.title: Diarization checkpoint publication
decisions.choice: Diarization writes each completed window's segments, centroids and proposal evidence into run-owned staging. Synchronize window payloads before appending a checksum-protected checkpoint record containing input hash, window index, epoch, runtime revision, parameters and artifact lengths. Recovery accepts the valid prefix and discards unfinished window tails. Persist all centroids on disk, with a 256-entry in-memory cache and paged candidate scanning. Cache overflow evicts an entry without deleting evidence or forcing a speaker match. New clusters always receive new IDs.
decisions.rationale: Durable staging permits useful resumption while keeping partial output outside published History and notes. A memory cache limit must not become a limit on distinct speakers.

alternatives.option: Publish segment rows after each window
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplifies progress display but makes an incomplete analysis reachable as a result.

alternatives.option: Keep all cluster evidence in memory
alternatives.tradeoff: Accelerates matching but grows with meeting complexity and loses progress on interruption.

decisions.consequences: One final transaction streams the completed result and initial speaker revision into Store under I2. D-031 controls resumption; D-007 controls cancellation. Publication cleanup removes staging after commit. Repeated crashes preserve only validated completed windows. Candidate scanning can become slower as speakers accumulate and remains preemptible.
decisions.reconsider_when: A tested incremental diarizer supplies equivalent persistent checkpoints with lower matching cost.

coverage.explanation: Ordered application and website rules resolve conflicts, unavailable predicates fall through, and the selected mode remains visible and frozen for the run.
The built-in contracts specify permitted transformations and preserve dictated questions. Fidelity checks and review have defined limits and dispositions.
Application text, screen context and clipboard content have sampling bounds, instruction separation, retention ownership and permission-loss behavior.
Users control prompts, formatting and local model selections. Immutable revisions preserve the settings that produced each saved result.
Menu bar access, local microphone gain and player controls are defined. Automatic restoration requires continuing ownership; unsupported integrations retain explicit resumption.
Search, playback and reprocessing use immutable result chains. Retention and deletion invalidate active publication before physical cleanup.
Microphone, system audio and the declared audio/video import matrix share bounded ingest. Decoder extensions remain local, and imports preserve external sources.
Explicit selection, detection and English translation have separate compatibility and evaluation behavior. Derived output retains its source transcript.
Local speaker analysis produces uncertain labels and non-destructive proposals. Editable revisions support timestamped notes with identified inputs and bounded working memory.

Local acquisition, identity, compatibility and publication are defined across staged and installed assets. Shared storage survives concurrent use, and absent quality scores do not disable compatible imports.
Global toggle and push-to-talk include configurable per-mode bindings, stop-modifier submission intent and cancellation at every stage.
The movable panel remembers placement, distinguishes live provisional text from final output, reports failures and receives explicit preview capacity.

One executor applies target policy, selection-aware insertion and submission rules. Clipboard ownership and uncertain outcomes prevent automatic duplicate retries. Permission loss holds output and offers Copy.
Terminology bias, deterministic replacements and optional filler removal have explicit ordering and matching rules without a recognition guarantee.

open_questions.question: Do the selected pinned runtimes load and process correctly through container-local materialization in the signed XPC arrangement?
open_questions.resolution: F2 validates the concrete D-003 choice before runtime integration is accepted. This is an unperformed feasibility check, not an undecided access mechanism. Failure requires a compliant adapter change; if none can supply a required operation, that operation becomes blocking.

open_questions.question: Which model sizes and parameters provide acceptable recognition, rewriting and preview on the evaluation Mac?
open_questions.resolution: F1 replaces provisional D-027 charges and selects shipped defaults using the frozen practical and statistical criteria. The runtime choices and user-import behavior are already decided.

open_questions.question: Can the complete meeting stack operate acceptably on Intel Macs?
open_questions.resolution: This blocks claiming Intel support, not implementation of the specified arm64 evaluation build. Exercise whisper.cpp and llama.cpp on identified Intel hardware and establish a compatible local diarizer with bounded memory. Preserve meeting functionality when choosing that runtime.

open_questions.question: Which application controls provide supported insertion acknowledgment and submission semantics?
open_questions.resolution: F4 establishes a versioned support matrix. Generic insertion already has the unconfirmed outcome and user-review path in D-009. Tests alone do not create acknowledgment semantics or authorize automatic fallback.

open_questions.question: Which real players expose atomic conditional resumption with ownership evidence covering every intervening control action?
open_questions.resolution: Inspect documented integrations and test competing actions before enabling automatic resume for any adapter. D-025 already supplies explicit player-specific resumption, which satisfies unsupported-player behavior without assuming a readable position is ownership.

open_questions.question: Which exact diarization assets can be offered as optional downloads?
open_questions.resolution: Compile component-specific asset hashes and notices before adding catalog entries. Local import and the selected diarization runtime remain available independently of distribution permission.

open_questions.question: Do the proposed capture and long-input resource bounds hold under storage and inference contention?
open_questions.resolution: F3 and the resource protocol measure the selected PCM and windowing design. Correct scheduling, buffer bounds or adapters when evidence fails. Recording-duration caps and removal of live preview are not acceptable resolutions.
